title: Vertical growth of Moso bamboo relies on local sensing and growth stress
content: Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis), one of the tallest and fastest-growing grasses, produces hollow culms that can exceed 20 m in a single growing season (Chen et al. 2022). Such rapid elongation creates a structural challenge. A stem with a length:diameter ratio >100 should be prone to buckling or collapse. Yet bamboo remains upright, flexing under wind or snow but recovering its vertical posture with precision. Luan et al. (2025) show that this stability arises from a finely tuned system of local orientation sensing, internal growth stress, and structural reinforcement.
